text.en: Record the tune of Ye Banks and Braes o' Bonnie Doon in Sing, with the other parts playing.
text.es: Graba la melodía de Ye Banks and Braes o' Bonnie Doon en Cantar, con las demás voces sonando.

text.en: Burns wrote that the organist Stephen Clarke, "partly by way of joke", told James Miller "to keep to the black keys of the harpsichord, and preserve some kind of rhythm, and he would infallibly compose a Scots air". In a few days Miller produced "the rudiments of an air", which Clarke fashioned into this tune.
text.es: Burns escribió que el organista Stephen Clarke, "partly by way of joke" (medio en broma), le dijo a James Miller "to keep to the black keys of the harpsichord, and preserve some kind of rhythm, and he would infallibly compose a Scots air" (que tocara solo las teclas negras del clave y mantuviera algo de ritmo, y sin falta compondría un aire escocés). En pocos días Miller trajo "the rudiments of an air" (el esbozo de un aire), que Clarke convirtió en esta melodía.

source.en: William Stenhouse, Illustrations of the Lyric Poetry and Music of Scotland (Edinburgh: Blackwood, 1853), pp. 346 and 347, quoting Burns's letter to George Thomson of November 1794, read from the scan
source.es: William Stenhouse, Illustrations of the Lyric Poetry and Music of Scotland (Edimburgo: Blackwood, 1853), pp. 346 y 347, citando la carta de Burns a George Thomson de noviembre de 1794, leído en el escaneo
